prompt: The moving_average implementation has an off-by-one defect. Reproduce it with the existing tests, make the smallest correct fix, and run the full test suite. Do not only explain the patch.

result.text:
Reproduced the off-by-one defect by running the existing test suite: `test_all_complete_windows_are_returned` and `test_equal_window_length_returns_one_average` both failed because `moving_average` returned one fewer window than expected.

Root cause: the range in the list comprehension was `range(len(values) - window)`, which excludes the final complete window. For `[1,2,3,4]` with window 2 it produced only indices 0,1 (missing index 2 → 3.5), and for window == len(values) it produced zero windows instead of one.

Fix (smallest targeted change in `src/window.py`): changed the range to `range(len(values) - window + 1)` so every complete sliding window is included. Integer validation and existing exceptions were preserved; no dependencies added.

Verified by running `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` — all 3 tests pass (OK).
